records.name: Proteomics & phosphoproteomics
records.tldr: These methods measure proteins or selected signals derived from them. Some also measure chemical modifications, which need to be interpreted separately from protein amount.
records.summary: Mass-spectrometry and antibody-based methods measure different protein-derived signals under defined workflows. A primary yeast study measured protein expression alongside phosphorylation and showed why a changed phosphopeptide signal can reflect protein abundance as well as phosphorylation. That methodological result is not a validated cancer-treatment rule. Targeted plasma-protein assays likewise require evidence about recovery, calibration and quantitative range. A protein measurement, modification-site signal, functional pathway dependence and prediction of treatment benefit are distinct claims. Beausoleil and colleagues introduced the Ascore, a probability-based score for how likely a phosphorylation site is correctly localised from site-determining ions in tandem mass spectra, alongside a target-decoy measure of dataset error (2006). In yeast, 25 per cent of seemingly differential phosphopeptides were attributable to changes in protein expression once phosphopeptide ratios were calibrated by protein levels (Wu and colleagues, 2011). In human ovarian tumour and breast cancer xenograft tissue collected without vascular interruption, rapid phosphorylation changes were seen in up to 24 per cent of the phosphoproteome after defined ischaemic intervals, while the global proteome and most of more than 25,000 quantified phosphosites were unchanged after 60 minutes; phosphopeptides in that study were enriched by immobilised metal (Fe3+) affinity chromatography before analysis (Mertins and colleagues, 2014).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). Kinases add phosphate and phosphatases remove it, as the existing phosphorylation record states, and a larger phosphopeptide signal is not a universal sign of greater activity. Enrichment changes what is recovered, so a phosphopeptide sample is not an unbiased count of all proteins. Site localisation is separate from peptide identification and carries its own confidence. A phosphopeptide intensity reflects the source-protein amount, the modified fraction and recovery, so intensity or fold change is not occupancy. A set of supported sites can inform a pathway hypothesis; it does not measure the pathway's rate, prove dependence or show benefit from a drug, and a kinase inferred from a pattern is not measured causality.

Fictional worked example with independent arithmetic. Parent-protein signal rises from 100 to 200 and phosphopeptide signal from 20 to 40, each on its own assay scale: 200 / 100 = 2 and 40 / 20 = 2, so the protein-adjusted relative change is 2 / 2 = 1. The raw 20 / 100 = 0.2 is not the fraction of protein molecules carrying the site, because recovery and response factors differ between the assays, and no activation or kinase-causality conclusion follows. A twofold phosphopeptide rise with a twofold parent-protein rise therefore does not show doubled activation.

Assay card in words (a reading guide). Measures and method: enriched phosphorylated peptides, identified sites and quantitative comparisons. Input and tissue cost: a protein extract with recorded collection and preservation; preparation consumes material, and enrichment may need more input than the companion total-protein assay. Output and units: phosphopeptide or site identifiers, localisation scores and relative intensities or ratios, with occupancy percentages only when specifically supported. Thresholds: separate identification error controls, localisation criteria and quantitative limits for the exact workflow. Failure modes: handling-induced change, incomplete recovery, ambiguous sites, low signal and unmeasured parent-protein change. Limits: no automatic activation, enzyme-of-origin, dependency or drug-benefit conclusion. Validation context: check reproducibility, timing controls and site-specific evidence.
records.principle: Measure protein-derived peptide or antibody signals, retaining assay specificity, preparation, calibration and the distinction between protein amount and modification state.
strengths: Measures protein-derived abundance and modification signals

records.name: Imaging mass cytometry
records.tldr: A way to stain a tumour slice for dozens of proteins at once using metal-tagged antibodies read by a mass spectrometer, giving a detailed map of which cells are where.
records.summary: The original imaging mass cytometry method combined metal-tagged antibodies with laser ablation and mass cytometry to map marker signals in tumor sections. Multiplexed ion beam imaging is a related approach that uses secondary ion mass spectrometry; the acquisition methods are distinct. Assigning tissue signals to individual cells also requires image analysis. Marker selection, antibody performance and segmentation affect what a reported cell profile means; a spatial association does not by itself establish a cellular mechanism or treatment response. The original imaging mass cytometry paper coupled immunohistochemical and immunocytochemical staining with high-resolution laser ablation to CyTOF mass cytometry, imaging 32 proteins and modifications at subcellular resolution in human breast cancer samples, with more than 100 markers possible given further isotopes; mass cytometry had previously been applied only to cell suspensions (Giesen and colleagues, 2014). Spillover between channels is reduced compared with dye-based flow cytometry but still exists, and a bead-based compensation workflow was developed to estimate and correct it in suspension and imaging mass cytometry, reducing the risk of reporting cell phenotype artefacts (Chevrier and colleagues, 2018).

notes: Reading guide (OnCo inference). The antibody panel selects what can be measured, so imaging mass cytometry is not untargeted proteomics. Laser ablation removes the sampled material, so the scanned region is consumed. Spatial proximity between marker-defined cells is a measured arrangement, not functional interaction, killing or patient benefit. Suspension mass cytometry shares the detection principle but loses the original arrangement.

Fictional worked example. A panel reports a rare double-positive cell population while one marker is extremely bright in a neighbouring mass channel. Before calling a new cell state, inspect channel interference and staining controls and overlay the cell boundaries, because spillover or a merged boundary can create apparent coexpression; even a corrected pattern still needs biological interpretation.

Figure reading (toy grid, light and dark renders agree): a stained section is sampled address by address, the address x2,y1 is recorded and material is removed; the channels for marker A (blue) and marker B (rose) are rebuilt on one grid, with the outlined tile at the same x2,y1 address in both; estimated cell borders need checking; and suspension cells lose this arrangement. Only selected markers are shown and nothing guarantees segmentation.

Assay card in words (a reading guide). Input and tissue cost: a compatible tissue section and a validated panel; ablation consumes the scanned region, and field choice and section area limit sampling. Output and units: metal-signal images, per-pixel or per-cell channel values, cell counts, densities per square millimetre and distances in micrometres; signals are not automatically absolute molecule counts. Controls: antibody validation and titration, positive and negative material, interference controls, instrument checks and boundary overlays. Thresholds: explicit marker, phenotype and spatial rules, with no universal immune-response cutoff. Failure modes: channel interference, weak staining, acquisition artefacts, unrepresentative fields, wrong boundaries and inconsistent analysis batches. Cannot tell you: unmeasured proteins, living-cell dynamics, antigen specificity, killing or benefit. Validation context: the panel and pipeline need technical validation.
records.principle: Imaging mass cytometry reads laser-ablated metal-tagged antibody signals from tissue; related ion-beam methods use a distinct acquisition approach.
strengths: Multiple markers localized on one tissue section
Supports cell profiling when staining and segmentation are validated
limitations: Slow acquisition and small fields of view

records.name: Neoantigen
records.tldr: An immune-recognition target arising from a sequence change in a tumor. Sequencing can suggest candidates, while display and recognition need their own evidence.
records.summary: Tumor sequencing can nominate altered protein sequences, and prediction methods can prioritize candidate peptides. Natural presentation and immune recognition are separate questions. A primary melanoma study recovered mutated HLA-associated peptides from native tumor material and tested selected peptides with immune assays. A consortium comparison likewise separated prediction features from measured immune interactions. A tumor-associated sequence alteration alone does not establish presentation, recognition, treatment benefit or a guarantee of healthy-tissue safety.

notes: Evidence for a candidate climbs through separate levels: a sampled tumour-specific alteration (is the altered message expressed?), a matched binding prediction (is it naturally processed and displayed?), a recovered HLA-associated peptide (which cells supplied it, and does a receptor recognise it?) and a controlled response to naturally presenting tumour (healthy-tissue specificity and patient benefit remain open). Altered splicing as well as substitutions, insertions, deletions and rearrangements can create candidate sequences, and not every unusual transcript is tumour-exclusive. Different HLA alleles present different fragments of one altered sequence, so one alteration can yield several candidates or none useful. Wells et al. (Cell 2020, PMID 33038342) tested 608 predicted epitopes for patient-matched T-cell binding; Litchfield et al. (Nature Communications 2020, PMID 32733040) linked frameshift mutations that escape nonsense-mediated decay to checkpoint outcomes in melanoma cohorts. Their performance figures do not transfer to other models, cancers or vaccines.

records.name: Immune measurements and product evidence
records.tldr: Each immune test or product-quality check answers a particular question. Connecting those questions helps explain how a proposed treatment moves from molecular measurements to evidence in people.
records.summary: This reading map links immune-assay readouts, antigen evidence, specimen preparation, RNA design, recognition modules and product quality. It is a set of evidence questions, not a required experimental sequence. Receptor binding, cytokine release, cell killing, lot potency and clinical benefit are different observations. A useful explanation names the sample, assay, model and comparison that support the claim, including the steps that remain untested.

records.name: ELISpot secretion assays
records.tldr: This test records spots where sampled cells release a chosen substance. A spot count describes secretion under the test conditions; other assays address recognition or killing.
records.summary: The original enzyme-linked immunospot method counted antibody-secreting cells; cytokine versions are used to examine stimulated immune-cell responses. Cancer Vaccine Consortium proficiency panels showed that sample handling, protocol choices and plate reading affected results. A result needs the measured molecule, stimulation, cell input, background and reporting rule. A positive secretion response alone does not show that the sampled cells recognize or kill an unmodified tumor.

notes: Method card, what it measures: cells that secrete a chosen molecule, most often interferon gamma, under defined stimulation, counted as spots on an antibody-coated membrane. How: capture antibodies hold the released molecule near the cell, the cells are removed and detection reagents make localised spots visible. Input: viable cells, often PBMCs, allocated to the test. Prior culture expansion changes the measured population, and the cells are removed before the membrane spots are read. Output: spot-forming units per stated number of input cells, with background handling stated. Thresholds: response and quality rules fixed in advance for that assay and study, so one paper's positivity rule is not imported into another laboratory's report. Failure modes: high background, dead cells, weak stimulation, merged spots, inconsistent counting or failed controls. It cannot tell each receptor's target, natural tumour recognition, safety in healthy tissue or clinical benefit.

Fictional arithmetic: wells with 100,000 input cells give 30 spots after peptide stimulation and 5 spots with vehicle. Background-subtracted, that is 30 minus 5 = 25 spots per 100,000 cells, or 250 spot-forming units per million input cells. This is an arithmetic summary and not a positivity cut-off, replicates, positive controls and a prespecified response rule still apply, and in mixed PBMCs it is not the frequency of a particular T-cell subset. If the cells came from an expanded culture, the number describes the cultured cells and not the responding fraction of the original blood draw.

What the evidence does and does not support: the interferon gamma ELISpot is described as measuring the difference in the number of cells secreting the molecule with and without peptide, and interferon gamma is produced predominantly by natural killer and natural killer T cells as well as Th1 CD4 and CD8 effector T cells, so a mixed-cell spot does not by itself name the responding cell (Wykes and Renia protocol). In HIV vaccine research robust ELISpot responses were induced in a phase IIb trial that lacked efficacy, which challenged the assay's predictive power (Streeck 2009), and a validation in cynomolgus monkeys for responses to viral vector antigens (Yang 2022) validates that preparation and species and not cancer efficacy. Peptide added to cells can bypass the tumour's own processing and presentation, so a peptide response needs a separate bridge to natural tumour recognition.

Receptor sequencing asks which receptor sequences are represented and in what relative abundance. ELISpot asks how many input cells release the chosen molecule under the stated stimulation. An expanded sequence does not establish that it caused a spot, and a spot in mixed cells does not identify a receptor sequence. Connecting identity to recognition or killing requires additional experiments with suitable controls.

Spot size or intensity is not a measure of target-cell killing. A negative result remains bounded by the number and condition of input cells, the stimulus, chosen secreted molecule, culture history and response rule; it is not a census of every responding cell in the body. Assay reproducibility and a cancer-treatment benefit claim need separate evidence.

records.name: Intracellular cytokine staining
records.tldr: This test measures signaling proteins retained inside stimulated cells and identifies which stained cell groups produced them. The result describes a response in the assay.
records.summary: An original multiparameter flow-cytometry study detected intracellular cytokine accumulation after antigen stimulation and measured several cytokines in individual cells. That study concerned viral responses, not cancer-treatment prediction. The stimulated material, measured cytokines, cell groups and analysis gates define the result. Cytokine production is distinct from direct measurement of target-cell death, and assay validation does not by itself establish clinical benefit.

notes: Method card, what it measures: cytokines retained inside cells during a defined assay, so a response can be assigned to stained cell populations. How: cells get a defined stimulus, a protein-transport inhibitor is present for a stated window so newly made cytokines accumulate, the cells are fixed and made permeable, and flow cytometry reads cytokine stains beside population markers, with a viability stain applied before fixation. Input: viable blood or tissue cells, with separate aliquots per stimulus, and fixed cells cannot go on to living-cell assays. Output: percent cytokine-positive cells within a named parent population, or percent with stated cytokine combinations. Controls: unstimulated or vehicle, a positive stimulation, viability and recovery, single-stain and staining-boundary controls. It cannot tell natural tumour presentation, direct target-cell killing, receptor sequence identity or clinical benefit.

Precision evidence: in a study among laboratories involved in HIV clinical trials, using a common protocol and a cytomegalovirus pp65 peptide mix, mean inter-laboratory coefficients of variation ranged from 17% to 44% depending on sample type and analysis method, cryopreserved PBMC gave lower variation than whole blood, and centralised analysis with a dynamic gating template cut it by 5% to 20%. Variation was lowest (18% to 24%) for samples with more than 0.5% interferon gamma positive T cells and highest (57% to 82%) for samples below 0.1%, so gating is a major source of variability and precision falls as the responding frequency falls (Maecker 2005). That study supports protocol and gating consistency and does not validate every panel, stimulus or disease.

Fictional interpretation: a report finds cells positive for both interferon gamma and tumour necrosis factor after peptide stimulation. They are double-cytokine-positive under that assay and may not be called tumour-killing, because natural tumour recognition and death of appropriate targets need separate tests, and a strong response to a broad positive control confirms assay responsiveness and not recognition of the intended peptide. Polyfunctional means meeting the assay's rules for several measured functions, so it always needs its panel and stimulus attached, and a stained subset can contain many receptors.

The stimulus changes the question. Added peptide can bypass some processing steps; whole protein needs suitable antigen-presenting cells and processing, while broad stimulation tests responsiveness without identifying the intended antigen. The 2021 flow-cytometry guidelines describe brefeldin A and monensin as transport inhibitors and explain that their choice and exposure window can affect what is measured. Intracellular accumulation after inhibition is not a measurement of how much cytokine reached the surrounding medium.

Cytokine-positive percentages need a named parent gate, and fluorescence intensity uses instrument-dependent units. Poor recovery, handling delays, signal overlap, altered staining after fixation or permeabilisation, background and scarce events can make a small positive population unstable, and inhibitor timing belongs to the protocol. Minimum event counts, positivity boundaries and clinical interpretation need validation for the panel, stimulus and population; there is no universal double-positive percentage that proves tumour killing or treatment benefit.

records.name: Peptide-HLA multimer staining
records.tldr: This test labels cells whose receptors bind a particular displayed peptide under the assay conditions. It helps identify a binding population that can then be studied for function.
records.summary: The original peptide-MHC tetramer study made soluble multimeric peptide-display complexes to identify antigen-specific T cells. Binding correlated with cytotoxicity in the tested systems, but those observations are different measurements. The chosen peptide and HLA molecule define which interaction is tested. Detecting multimer-binding cells does not by itself establish natural display of that peptide by a tumor, successful target-cell killing or a clinical treatment effect.

notes: Method card, what it measures: binding of cells to a specified peptide held by a specified HLA allele, under the staining conditions. How: HLA molecules are assembled with the selected peptide and several copies are attached to a labelled scaffold (a tetramer is one format), cells are exposed and analysed, usually by flow cytometry, with viable-cell and gate selection. Input: blood or tissue cells, where staining uses a defined aliquot and compatibility with later living-cell assays depends on the preparation, and the reagent must match both peptide and allele. Thresholds: gate and positivity rules need background and reagent controls, and no universal percentage shows efficacy. Failure modes: nonspecific binding, weak binding, dead cells, a wrong or poorly formed reagent, chain differences or sampling loss. It cannot tell cytokine response, tumour-cell killing, healthy-tissue specificity or benefit.

Denominators, fictional arithmetic: 100 stained cells among 10,000 gated CD8 T cells is 1%, and the same 100 among 40,000 viable acquired cells is 0.25%. Both are correct and answer different denominator questions, and neither is a body-wide census or a killing rate. A tetramer-negative result is not a census of every possible relevant receptor, because some receptors bind too weakly for a given staining method, and HLA restriction belongs to the peptide-HLA pair and not the peptide alone.

What the evidence shows: in the original report, tetramers of HLA-A2 with two HIV-derived peptides or an influenza A matrix peptide bound peptide-specific cytotoxic T cells in vitro and T cells from the blood of HIV-infected people, and binding in general correlated well with cytotoxicity assays (Altman 1996). That is a correlation in those systems and not a rule that binding equals killing for an arbitrary tumour peptide. Tetramers are made by mixing biotinylated MHC with fluorescent streptavidin, and a later method made them with small-molecule fluorophores (Ramachandiran 2007), so reagent preparation is a source of variation. An observed stain shows binding under the tested conditions and does not show natural processing and display of that pair by a tumour.

Connecting assays is an inference task. A multimer-binding cell with no measured cytokine response need not identify one failed biological step: reagent performance, viability, stimulation, measurement window and each assay's threshold can differ. A cytokine response still does not directly measure target-cell death. Compatible cell sorting and receptor sequencing can connect binding to an operational receptor identity, but natural tumour presentation, recognition and killing remain separate questions to test.

Avidity describes the combined strength of multiple contacts. Multimerising peptide-HLA ligands can make binding detectable when an individual receptor-ligand contact is weak; the 2021 guidelines also caution that more multimerisation does not always improve detection. The measured output is a gate-defined binding fraction or, with a suitable counting method, a count. Reagent, viability and background controls support that binding measurement, which still requires separate validation before use for treatment selection.

records.name: Immune-cell cytotoxicity assays
records.tldr: These experiments measure whether immune cells cause death of specified target cells. The target cells, comparison conditions and timing are part of the result.
records.summary: A primary flow-cytometry method distinguished labeled target cells from immune effector cells and measured target death while characterizing the effector population. The study examined how timing and the effector-to-target ratio affected the assay. Degranulation markers provide a related functional readout, but they measure a step preceding cytolysis. Killing of a laboratory target does not establish recognition of every tumor cell or benefit in the person receiving a treatment.

notes: Method card, what it measures: whether specified effector cells cause death of specified target cells under controlled laboratory conditions, at a stated effector-to-target ratio and time. Readouts: flow cytometry that separates labelled targets from effectors and uses death-associated staining, release assays, or imaging over time. A fall in a metabolic or growth signal can reflect slowed growth and not death, so it needs validation as evidence of killing. Controls: target-only survival wells, effector identification and viability, a positive-control response, irrelevant or antigen-negative targets and suitable antigen or presentation perturbations, plus maximum release where relevant. Failure modes: high spontaneous death, mistaken target identity, aggregates, dye transfer, artificial loading, mismatched ratios or a readout that mainly measures growth.

Background arithmetic, fictional: matched wells of 100 identifiable targets show 30% death without effectors and 40% with them at the same 2-hour endpoint. Raw death is 40%, but 30% occurs without effectors, so the excess is 40 minus 30 = 10 percentage points. That excess is associated with the tested condition and does not identify which deaths the effectors caused, and calling the result 40% immune killing is not justified. A control-normalised specific-lysis formula gives a different quantity from an excess-death calculation, so the method has to be named, and a high baseline death can make the experiment unsuitable.

Scope of the methods: a flow-based assay labels targets with a dye, adds a dead-cell stain and analyses released nuclei, which lowers errors from target-effector aggregates, and it reported four nuclear staining patterns separating target and effector nuclei and live and dead cells (Rabinovich 2019). A peptide-pulsed target assay compares CFSE-low peptide-loaded and CFSE-high unloaded CD4 T-cell targets and calculates lytic units from specific lysis at several ratios (Noto 2013), so its result belongs to that artificial peptide loading, which can bypass the tumour's own processing. Degranulation (CD107 exposure) preceded cytolysis and was concordant with interferon gamma in the original report, and is distinct from completed target death (Betts 2003). Model-specific killing does not show trafficking, persistence, healthy-tissue safety or patient benefit.

Keep the identities and preparation of both effector and target cells, whether a cell line, engineered target or patient-derived preparation, together with medium, effector-to-target ratio and exposure time. Culture can change the tested population. The output might be a fraction of identified targets dead, a viable target count, release under a specified normalisation, or a time curve; these are different quantities. A negative is interpretable only when cell health, target suitability and controls support the experiment, and no universal laboratory killing cut-off establishes clinical efficacy. Reproducibility and biological specificity need checking for the specimen, model and intended claim.

records.name: T-cell receptor repertoire sequencing
records.tldr: Receptor sequencing records the immune-receptor sequences sampled from a population of cells. It can track which sequences are present and how their measured abundance changes.
records.summary: An original sequencing study quantified rearranged T-cell receptor beta-chain sequences to examine repertoire diversity. A beta-chain repertoire is a sampled molecular measurement, not a complete map of paired receptors or the antigens they recognize. The specimen, sequencing method and definition of a clonotype belong with the result. Following a sequence over time is distinct from demonstrating its antigen specificity or the function of the cells that carry it.

notes: Beta match, alpha hidden, fictional: three cells carry beta chains B, B and C, so a bulk beta-chain view lists B, B, C and loses the alpha chains. The paired view keeps alpha X with beta B, alpha Y with beta B and alpha Z with beta C, so the shared beta B does not make alpha X and alpha Y equal. Single-cell methods that sequence the alpha and beta genes of individual T cells retain each pair and can be combined with function-related gene expression, and the same TCR sequence can sit in functionally different cells (Han 2014). A bulk method profiles a mixed sample, often one chain, whereas TIRTL-seq generates paired alpha and beta repertoire data at cohort scale and is distinguished from bulk single-chain data and from single-cell throughput limits (Pogorelyy 2026). Paired identity plus an expression program is more context and is still not evidence of the receptor's antigen.

Frequency arithmetic, fictional: clonotype A is 10 of 10,000 sampled receptor units at baseline (0.1%) and 20 of 1,000 later (2%). The measured relative frequency rose twentyfold, but these are sampled receptor units and not a census of cells, and other populations contracting, different sampling and method effects can change frequency. Read counts are not always cell counts, because preparation, amplification and transcript abundance can change them, and absolute expansion needs compatible cell-number evidence. A sequence overlap between blood and tumour is detected overlap under a clonotype definition and is not a target, and antigen specificity needs a matching controlled recognition experiment.

Assay card: measures receptor identities, usually by the complementarity-determining region 3 of the variable region, and their measured representation in the sampled population. How: extract nucleic acid, amplify or capture receptor regions, sequence, then group and count under stated rules, which may use nucleotide or amino-acid sequence, gene segments, one chain or paired chains. Input: blood cells or tissue nucleic acid for bulk methods and compatible cell preparations for single-cell methods, and preparation consumes material. A high-resolution human repertoire method reported chain diversity without sequence-associated or quantitative restrictions (Ruggiero 2015). Failure modes: poor material, shallow sampling, amplification bias, chain mismatch, inconsistent definitions and batch effects. It cannot tell every receptor's target, tissue position, killing or benefit, and a research method is not automatically a treatment-selection test.

Nucleotide and amino-acid clonotypes need not be the same grouping. The standard genetic code assigns several codons to the same amino acid, so different nucleotide sequences can encode the same receptor segment; amino-acid identity alone is not proof of one cellular lineage. MIGEC introduced molecular-identifier groups to correct PCR and sequencing errors in antibody and T-cell receptor repertoire profiling (Shugay 2014). Such error correction does not restore molecules absent from the sample. Report which chain, grouping rule and abundance unit the method actually used.

A repertoire report can give a clonotype list, relative frequencies, diversity, clonality and overlap, but there is no universal expansion or clonality threshold that proves tumour specificity. A sequence found in dissociated tumour material does not locate its cell inside a cancer-cell nest. Not detected means absent from the assay result under its sampling and calling rules, while an observed overlap or change nominates a receptor for a separate controlled recognition experiment.

records.name: T-cell receptor repertoire diversity and clonality
records.tldr: Repertoire measures describe how many receptor identities are sampled and how unevenly they are represented. A dominant sequence does not tell us what its cells recognize.
records.summary: Repertoire sequencing can describe richness and the distribution of sampled receptor sequences. Those summaries depend on the sampled population and the way receptor identities and counts are defined; the original sequencing study found diversity estimates that differed from earlier methods. A repertoire dominated by a clone is a distributional observation. It is distinct from proving tumor specificity, a malignant clone or successful tumor killing, each of which needs additional evidence.

notes: The repertoire is a distribution of receptor identities and abundances in a stated population and time. A clone is a cellular lineage; a clonotype is an operational sequence grouping. Single-chain labels and paired identities have different resolution. V(D)J assembly and thymic selection contribute diversity, while expansion changes abundance; diversity and total T-cell count are different quantities.

Blood, tumour and lymph nodes sample overlapping but different populations. Infection, therapy, age and movement can change a sample; absence from one tube may reflect sampling or detection rather than whole-body absence. A pretreatment blood sample is not a complete stored repertoire. Lower measured diversity after infection may reflect a vigorous response and does not establish cancer specificity, vaccine causation or uniformly worse immunity.

Fictional matched receptor samples contain 10 clonotype A cells among 1,000 T cells (1%) and 10 among 100 (10%). The sampled count remains 10; the changed denominator drives the larger fraction. Absolute expansion requires comparable sampling and calibrated counts, and neither frequency identifies antigen. State sampling depth, chain definition, compartment, method and timing.

Metrics and arithmetic, fictional: with natural logarithms Shannon entropy is H = minus the sum of p times ln p, and one normalised clonality convention is 1 minus H / ln K for K observed clonotypes greater than one. Four clonotypes at 25, 25, 25 and 25 of 100 measured molecules give H = ln 4 = 1.386 and clonality 0. The same four at 70, 10, 10 and 10 give H = 0.940, clonality 1 minus 0.940 / 1.386 = 0.32, and an effective number of clonotypes exp(H) = 2.56. Richness is four in both, so many identities can coexist with strong dominance. Software may report Shannon entropy, its exponential or a normalised score, and these are not interchangeable: in the VDJtools documentation the Shannon-Wiener index returns the exponent of the entropy and the normalised index returns the entropy divided by the log of the clonotype count, which is evenness and not 1 minus that ratio, so a clonality built as 1 minus normalised entropy is a different number from either.

Share against count, fictional: clonotype A is 30 of 100 measured molecules, 30%, and later 30 of 50, 60%. Its measured count did not rise, the total fell, and its relative frequency doubled, so relative enrichment is not absolute expansion and the molecule counts are not blood cell counts. In a published analysis pipeline, clonality was identified as a robust key metric and first choice for measuring TCR repertoire diversity, and in prostate cancer patients given sipuleucel-T the pipeline detected changes in sequence frequency and diversity in blood and prostate tissue (Zhang 2017); that is a methods and example study and sets no response threshold. A diversity-analysis software suite reports repertoire comparison and diversity outputs (Shugay 2015), and formulas, software settings and subsampling depth have to be stated.

Measurement card: input is a sequencing-derived clonotype table and the calculation consumes no further tissue, though the upstream assay consumes its sample. Output units are a count for richness, dimensionless values for entropy and normalised clonality, and an effective clonotype count for effective diversity. Controls are matched compartments and handling, chain definition, error filtering, abundance units (reads, corrected molecules or cells are not automatically equivalent), depth assessment and replicates or resampling. Subsampling to a comparable depth helps assess sampling effects but cannot recover cells never sampled. A clonality summary does not identify what the receptors recognise, whether cells killed tumour, or whether treatment helped, and there is no universal clonality score that means an immune therapy is working.

Effective-diversity measures weight a distribution differently. For the inverse-Simpson convention, define D as the sum of squared clonotype fractions and report 1 / D: four equal fractions of 0.25 give 4, whereas 0.70, 0.10, 0.10 and 0.10 give 1 / 0.52, about 1.92. This differs from the Shannon effective diversity of about 2.56 for the same uneven distribution. A fictional sample containing only A and B at 50 molecules each has richness 2 and equal weights; low richness does not imply unequal weights.

For one observed clonotype, the expression 1 minus H / ln K divides by ln 1, which is zero. Report how the software handles that case rather than silently applying the formula. Low input, unequal depth, amplification bias, sequence errors, changing mixtures and inconsistent clonotype definitions can alter the result. Keep the software version, formula, filtering, input, compartment and abundance units, and inspect the distribution alongside the summary. Analytical reproducibility of a repertoire statistic does not establish a prognostic association or predict treatment benefit.

records.name: Peripheral blood mononuclear cell specimens
records.tldr: This blood-cell preparation contains lymphocytes and monocytes used in many immune tests. Collection and handling affect which cells and responses can be measured.
records.summary: The National Library of Medicine distinguishes mononuclear leukocytes from granulocytes and from monocytes alone. A primary study of immune monitoring in HIV vaccine research found that processing and cryopreservation conditions affected cell recovery, viability and measured antigen responses. Those were assay findings, not a validated cancer-treatment predictor. A blood preparation also samples a different compartment from a tumor biopsy; the specimen and handling conditions belong with its interpretation.

notes: What the fraction is: peripheral blood mononuclear cells are circulating white blood cells with a single unsegmented nucleus, mainly lymphocytes and monocytes, with T, B and natural killer cells among them, isolated by layering anticoagulated blood over a density-separation medium and collecting the interface. Most conventional granulocytes and red cells separate elsewhere, but recovery is incomplete, so platelets, red cells or low-density granulocytes can contaminate a preparation, and the label PBMC does not guarantee purity. The classic density-gradient method dates from 1968 (Boyum 1968). Isolation selects a recoverable blood fraction and does not sample tumour or give a complete immune census.

Handling is evidence: in HIV vaccine assay studies, the time from venipuncture to cryopreservation was the most important parameter, and blood processed at 24 hours compared with within 8 hours lost on average about 8% of PBMC viability, about 32% of cell recovery and 36% to 56% of interferon gamma T-cell frequencies by ELISpot, which led the authors to recommend cryopreservation within 8 hours (Bull 2007). That is a finding for those protocols and assays and is not a universal schedule for cancer assays. A rapidly processed baseline and a delayed follow-up can therefore confound a biological comparison, and a high viability percentage alone does not show that every population or function was preserved.

Preparation card: input is anticoagulated blood or a blood-cell collection product and separation processes that aliquot and retains a selected cell fraction for compatible downstream assays. Output is recovered cell number, viable-cell percentage, recovery after thawing and measured population fractions, with cells per original blood volume needing a documented calculation. Controls are collection and processing timestamps, anticoagulant, storage, counting and viability methods and matched handling across time points. Thresholds are acceptance rules set for the intended downstream assay and not one universal quality number. Fictional case: two tubes have equally high viability but one recovered far fewer monocytes, so they are not automatically interchangeable for a whole-protein stimulation assay, because monocytes can contribute antigen presentation and viability does not show composition.

The usable input for a downstream assay is the recovered viable cell preparation, not simply the volume of blood drawn. Fresh isolation, freezing, thawing, washing and any rest period define a sequence of selections, so record recovery, population composition and purity as well as viability. The Cytiva density-separation handbook describes the mononuclear interface, platelet carryover and possible immature-granulocyte contamination in pathological blood. That manufacturer method source does not validate every cancer assay, and an inadequate number of the relevant cells can make a rare-response experiment uninformative.

A stored PBMC sample is a finite specimen. It does not establish immune infiltration of a tumour, preserve every function or population equally, identify antigen specificity, or guarantee enough material for every later test. In the fictional equal-viability comparison, losing monocytes can affect a whole-protein stimulation because antigen-presenting-cell composition matters; viability alone does not establish interchangeable inputs. Fit and acceptance rules belong to the intended downstream assay.

records.tldr: A peptide can bind a display molecule, be displayed by a cell, or be recognized by an immune receptor. These are different questions that require different evidence.
records.summary: Binding prediction estimates one part of antigen selection. Immunopeptidomics examines peptides recovered with HLA molecules, while immune assays investigate receptor binding and functional responses. A primary melanoma study directly identified naturally presented mutated peptides and separately tested their immunogenicity. A consortium study likewise evaluated prediction against measured immune interactions. A candidate supported at one stage should retain that evidence level rather than being described as a demonstrated therapeutic target.

records.tldr: The immunopeptidome is the collection of peptides associated with immune display molecules in a particular biological setting. A measurement recovers a view of that collection through a defined assay.

Direct analysis of native melanoma tissue identified HLA-associated peptides, including some containing tumor mutations. What is recovered depends on the tissue and analytical workflow. The observed collection should retain its sample and method, and identifying a displayed peptide remains distinct from showing an immune response to it.

notes: The immunopeptidome is a biological repertoire in a defined cell population and context; an immunopeptidomics list is a method-dependent subset recovered and identified from a sample. Class I and class II repertoires are separate, and a protein can be abundant while a derived peptide is poorly generated, loaded or retained. Inflammatory signals changed peptide patterns in cancer cell lines (Chong et al., 2018, ovarian cancer cells and interferon gamma, PMID 29242379; Javitt et al., 2019, lung cancer cells and TNF-alpha and interferon gamma acting through HLA-B, PMID 30833945), which shows context-dependent remodelling and not that inflammation adds useful targets. Whole-lysate capture can recover intracellular as well as surface complexes, mixed tissue adds cancer, immune and stromal sources, relative instrument intensity is not surface copies per cell, and a reported sequence can be misassigned (Wilhelm et al., 2021, PMID 34099720). Method B identifying 1,200 peptides against method A's 800 (fictional) shows no biological difference. Sarkizova et al. (2020) gives allele-dependent repertoires from mono-allelic lines.

records.name: Immunopeptidomics
records.tldr: This laboratory approach identifies peptides recovered with immune display molecules. It supplies evidence about peptide presentation in the material that was analyzed.
records.summary: A primary melanoma study used mass spectrometry to identify HLA-associated peptides from native tumor tissue and then evaluated selected mutated peptides with immune assays. This is stronger evidence of natural presentation in the sampled material than a binding prediction alone. The analytical observation still has a defined specimen and workflow. It does not automatically establish the abundance of a ligand on every cancer cell, receptor recognition or a treatment effect. A published protocol isolates MHC-peptide complexes by immunoaffinity capture, dissociates the peptides by acid denaturation, fractionates them by HPLC and identifies them by nano-UPLC tandem mass spectrometry, from cell lines and tissues (Purcell and colleagues, 2019). Capture starts from mild-detergent solubilised lysates (Chong and colleagues, 2018; Sarkizova and colleagues, 2020 immunoprecipitated HLA from soluble lysates), so a lysate is not a surface-only survey, and in multi-allele samples a peptide was assigned to the best-scoring allele or alleles by computation (Sarkizova and colleagues, 2020). Identification depends on the analysis: a deep-learning model trained on more than 300,000 synthetic peptides improved HLA peptide identification up to 7-fold and indicated that 87 per cent of the proposed proteasomally spliced HLA peptides may be incorrect (Wilhelm and colleagues, 2021). A quantitative tissue study isolated peptide-HLA complexes from snap-frozen tissue and used formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded blocks only for histology (Science Translational Medicine, 2022).

Fictional worked example. A specimen yields peptide A but not peptide B. A has measured support in that preparation. For B, ask whether its allele was recovered, whether the altered sequence was searchable and whether sensitivity was adequate; 'A detected, B absent everywhere' is stronger than the experiment supports. If B is simply missing from the search database it could not have been identified as configured, so its absence is not a clean biological negative, and correcting the database does not by itself guarantee recovery or prove natural display.

Reading guide: binding prediction estimates a model output, whereas immunopeptidomics identifies recovered peptides, and total-protein measurements are a different question from HLA-associated fragments (a protein can be abundant without any of its peptides being displayed, an inference); presentation, immune response and efficacy are three separate claims.

Measurement card in words (a reading guide). Input: which tissue preparation and preservation are compatible, and how much material is consumed. Output and units: peptide identities and unique-sequence counts; instrument intensities are method-dependent and not copies per cell. Identification threshold: the sequence database, the false-discovery rule (spectrum or peptide level) and the supporting spectra. Coverage: which HLA classes and alleles were captured and which allele assignments were measured or inferred. Material and cost: protocol-specific input, preservation, consumption, turnaround and analysis cost, requested before a scarce specimen is used. Validation: recovery, reproducibility and reference-peptide checks for the method. Failure modes: low input, poor recovery, mixed cell populations, database gaps and wrong sequence assignments. Limits: non-detection does not prove absence and detection does not prove safe recognition; there is no universal tissue requirement or detection threshold.

records.name: Peptide-HLA binding and ligand prediction
records.tldr: A computer model can prioritize peptides expected to bind an immune display molecule or appear among its ligands. The prediction helps select candidates for testing.
records.summary: NetMHCpan-4.0 combined peptide-binding affinity data with eluted-ligand data, which also contain information about processing and natural presentation. Those training signals and prediction tasks should be distinguished. A consortium comparison assessed candidate tumor epitopes using measured immune interactions and developed improved prioritization features. A model score is a prediction with a validation setting; it is not an observation of peptide display, tumor recognition or patient benefit. The NetMHCpan-4.1 documentation expresses binder thresholds as percentile rank, the position of a predicted score against the scores of random natural peptides, and lets the user set the strong and weak binder thresholds, so a 0.4 per cent rank places a candidate within the top 0.4 per cent of that reference and is not a 99.6 per cent probability of presentation, recognition or benefit. The server predicts binding of a peptide to an MHC molecule of known sequence, and its model is trained on more than 850,000 binding-affinity and mass-spectrometry eluted-ligand peptides, two different training signals (Reynisson and colleagues, 2020). A model trained on more than 185,000 peptides eluted from 95 single-allele cell lines improved prediction of presented peptides (Sarkizova and colleagues, 2020). In a consortium study, 608 predicted epitopes were then tested for T-cell binding in patient-matched samples, a separate experiment from the prediction (Wells and colleagues, 2020), so expression, processing, display, T-cell receptor recognition and sparing of healthy tissue remain to be shown after a favourable score.

notes: Assay distinction. A predicted binding IC50 estimates a competitive-binding assay endpoint. An IC50 depends on the assay conditions and is not automatically an equilibrium dissociation constant. Cer and colleagues' 2009 IC50-to-Ki tool calculates binding or inhibition constants using the interaction mechanism, concentrations and other assumptions; this is a biochemical distinction, not validation of an HLA model or a measure of cancer-cell growth inhibition. Reading guide (OnCo inference): Record the model and version, allele, peptide length, prediction task, units, reference distribution and threshold beside every score, and do not put a rank and an IC50 in one unlabelled column. A threshold is a selection rule for a stated workflow and cannot repair the wrong allele or an unsupported task. Inputs are peptide or source-protein sequences and an exact allele; scoring uses no tumour tissue; held-out validation, allele coverage and the endpoint (binding, recovery or T-cell recognition) decide what a good score means.

Figure reading (fictional numbers, light and dark renders agree): a 1,000-score reference for HLA-A*02:01 9-mer peptides has bin counts 250, 240, 200, 130, 80, 50, 30, 16 and 4, which sum to 1,000. Four reference scores lie beyond the candidate boundary, so 4 / 1,000 x 100 = 0.4 per cent. A separate binding-affinity output of 40 nM is a predicted IC50. Neither value observes display.

Fictional worked example. Candidate A has an eluted-ligand rank of 0.4 per cent and candidate B a predicted binding IC50 of 40 nM. The numbers come from different outputs with different units and tasks, so neither ranks the candidates against each other or shows tumour coverage; request matched outputs for the relevant allele and method, and test display and recognition separately.

Output table in words. Predicted binding IC50 in nanomolar units: lower values mean stronger predicted competitive binding for that output, and it is not a measured concentration, an equilibrium dissociation constant or a functional T-cell response. Percentile rank: a lower rank places the candidate nearer the model's stronger-scoring reference peptides, and it is not a percent chance of tumour killing or the fraction of tumour cells covered.

records.name: Immunodominance
records.tldr: Immune responses to a set of possible targets are often uneven. Some epitopes attract a stronger measured response than others in the same setting.
records.summary: A primary mouse experiment showed that T-cell populations could compete for access to antigen-bearing presenting cells, changing responses to dominant and subdominant epitopes. That identifies one mechanism of immunodominance in the studied system. It does not supply a universal ranking of human tumor epitopes. The antigen design, presentation context and responding repertoire all need to remain attached to an observation of a dominant response.

notes: Immunodominance is a contextual hierarchy of measured responses, distinct from encoded target count and from epitope spreading. Presentation, precursor frequency, repertoire, priming, HLA, delivery, immune history, tissue and time can change the hierarchy. A favourable binding prediction does not establish immunogenicity, and more encoded targets do not guarantee balanced immunity or independent tumour coverage.

Naive precursor frequency is the starting abundance of cells with a relevant specificity. Mouse LCMV and human HLA-A2-restricted HCV experiments linked precursor frequencies to response hierarchies. Binding alone did not strictly predict the hierarchy. These studies provide no universal cancer-vaccine weights, human marker requirement or instruction to remove dominant clones.

Fictional matched IFN-gamma ELISpot means of 45, 11 and 5 spots for A, B and C, minus matched background 5, give 40, 6 and 0 spots per 200,000 plated PBMCs. A dominates that measured response. Protocol replicate and positivity rules classify C as undetectable. Zero adjusted spots do not prove absent tumour display or universal uselessness, nor do three encoded sequences imply three equally effective responses.

A measured hierarchy needs offered targets, compartment, cell denominator, baseline, timing, matched per-target stimulation, background and positive controls. Detection thresholds and in vitro expansion can alter apparent ranking. Peptide response is not evidence of natural tumour display or tumour-cell killing.

records.name: Epitope spreading
records.tldr: An immune response can broaden to recognize additional epitopes over time. Showing that broadening requires measurements of the added specificities.
records.summary: A follow-up study of a small melanoma neoantigen-vaccine cohort found persistent immune responses, evolving receptor clonotypes and evidence of responses beyond the original vaccine targets. The report provides clinical immune-monitoring evidence of spreading in that cohort. The response measurements are distinct from a randomized estimate of treatment benefit. Spreading should not be inferred solely from an increased total lymphocyte count or expansion of an unidentified receptor sequence.

notes: Epitope spreading is additional detected recognition beyond the initially targeted epitope set, potentially within one source protein or across proteins. More response to the same target is expansion. Responses to both directly encoded A and B do not themselves demonstrate spreading. Newly detected is not newly created: baseline sensitivity can miss pre-existing responsive cells.

Tumour injury can release additional antigen for uptake and presentation, but one follow-up response does not establish that entire causal chain. Define peptide-HLA targets and compare matched baseline and follow-up assays with background, presentation and cross-reactivity controls; assess intervening treatment. Vaccine recruitment or expansion does not normally rewrite mature TCRs. An immune response, including one to healthy self, does not establish recurrence prevention, safety or clinical benefit.

In a fictional A/B vaccine experiment, baseline C is undetectable and matched follow-up detects unencoded C, consistent with an additional detected specificity. The A-cell icons are qualitative, not counts. Ten additional receptor sequences without target testing demonstrate repertoire change, not recognition of C; causation and patient benefit remain separate questions.

records.name: Self-similarity and immune-recognition specificity
records.tldr: A receptor may recognize more than one related peptide. Target-selection evidence needs to address recognition of healthy tissue as well as the intended target.
records.summary: A primary investigation of an affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3-directed receptor identified cross-recognition of a peptide from titin after unexpected cardiac toxicity. This was a particular engineered-receptor program, not a toxicity rate for all T-cell therapies or neoantigen vaccines. It illustrates why target-gene expression and a sequence match alone are insufficient descriptions of receptor specificity. Proposed-target recognition and off-target recognition need evidence in relevant systems.

notes: Central and peripheral tolerance include distinct mechanisms. Kisielow and colleagues demonstrated deletion of self-reactive developing cells in an H-Y-receptor transgenic mouse model. Jenkins and Schwartz demonstrated antigen-related unresponsiveness after altered antigen presentation in mouse experiments, and Sakaguchi and colleagues linked a CD4/CD25 regulatory population to prevention of autoimmunity in mice. These are mechanistic examples, rather than universal human response or safety thresholds. A tumour-specific mutation can make a peptide distinguishable from its normal counterpart, but display and a responsive receptor are still needed, and there is no universal percentage of identity that makes a target safe. Higher receptor affinity is not automatically more selective. Receptors can cross-react with peptides from unrelated proteins, as in the titin peptide recognised by the MAGE-A3-directed receptor (Cameron et al., 2013, PMID 23926201; Linette et al., 2013, PMID 23770775). Luksza et al. (Nature 2022, PMID 35589842) modelled neoantigen quality, using non-selfness and selfness, in pancreatic cancer survivors; the model is not a clinical safety rule. In a loaded-peptide concentration series, compare mutant and normal peptides at the same concentration with the same HLA and responder; artificial loading leaves natural processing open and a response threshold is not a patient safety threshold.

records.name: Immunogenicity and clinical efficacy
records.tldr: An intervention can produce a measurable immune response. Whether it improves a clinical outcome is a separate question about people receiving the intervention.
records.summary: A phase 1 personal neoantigen-vaccine report and its follow-up examined immune responses in small melanoma cohorts. Such work can demonstrate biological activity, persistence and broadening of responses. It does not by itself isolate the treatment effect on recurrence or survival from other explanations. An immune-assay endpoint, a clinical outcome and a comparative efficacy estimate should retain their distinct definitions and study designs.

notes: Immunogenicity asks whether an intervention elicits an immune response; clinical efficacy asks what adding it changes in a defined clinical endpoint, population and comparison. An immune result can justify further investigation without settling whether adding the intervention improves outcomes. For a therapeutic cancer vaccine, antigen-stimulated secretion and recurrence over follow-up answer different questions. The immune result needs its specimen, stimulus, preparation, timing, controls and denominator. The clinical result needs the intervention components, comparator, outcome rule, starting clock, follow-up, missing-data handling, harms and uncertainty. A surrogate endpoint also needs evidence connecting it to clinical benefit in that setting. Comparing standard care plus vaccine with the same care without vaccine can address the addition. Randomisation strengthens attribution, while measurement quality and follow-up remain necessary. Even a clinical outcome difference does not identify the particular clone or immune mechanism that caused it. The FDA's 2018 endpoint guidance informs these general distinctions, rather than current regulatory or treatment advice.

ELISpot measures secretion under defined stimulation. Supplying peptide can bypass natural processing, and laboratory expansion changes which cells and states are measured. In the 2017 phase I melanoma vaccine study by Ott and colleagues, the selected assay passages distinguish direct ex vivo measurements from responses detected after peptide-driven expansion. That specific study supports assay interpretation; it is not an added-benefit comparison for every vaccine. A change in receptor frequency alone establishes neither antigen specificity nor vaccine-induced function, and a weak blood signal can miss responses in tissue. Natural tumour recognition, location, function and safety require their own evidence.

Consider a fictional single-arm vaccine study in which peptide-reactive cells appear and some participants later recur. The measured immune response can remain real. Recurrence does not identify whether natural antigen display, tissue access, cell state or immune escape limited its effect, and without a suitable clinical comparison the recurrence frequency cannot isolate the vaccine's contribution from standard care or selection. In a second fictional example, circulating tumour DNA becomes undetectable after standard treatment plus vaccine. This tumour-derived DNA result is not an immune measurement. Timing, treatment effects, sampling and detection limits prevent attributing clearance to the vaccine alone. These observations supply no calculable added-efficacy estimate and do not prove an effect of zero.

A related fictional example finds a clone becoming more frequent after treatment while circulating tumour DNA is no longer detected. This establishes a receptor-repertoire change alongside a tumour-DNA result, not that the clone eliminated the cancer. Relative frequency can rise because that clone increased, others declined, or both. Tumour specificity, function, causal attribution and assay detection limits remain separate questions, and timing, other treatments, shedding and sampling can also shape a tumour-DNA result. Suitable comparisons and target-specific experiments strengthen attribution; temporal coincidence alone does not supply it.

Assess suitability by documenting preservation, checking which cells are represented and applying quality checks for the intended assay or living-cell workflow. Sections, tissue pieces and cell aliquots are finite, and destructive quality checks also use material. Receiving-laboratory requirements and diagnostic priorities apply, rather than a universal test budget. Outdated inventories, unrecognised exhaustion, unsuitable regions and duplicated destructive work can waste material. Specimen governance supports reliable testing but is not itself a clinical biomarker and does not establish whether a test changes care or another procedure is appropriate.

records.name: RNA integrity and assay suitability
records.tldr: RNA quality measurements describe the condition of extracted RNA. Their usefulness depends on the measurement workflow the material will enter.
records.summary: The original RNA Integrity Number method summarized electrophoretic features to standardize quality assessment. DV200 describes the proportion of RNA fragments longer than 200 nucleotides. Comparisons of fixed and frozen tissue found that fragment-distribution measures and functional amplification assays could be more informative for particular workflows. The NCI preanalytical-variables study likewise found method-dependent sensitivity to handling effects. An integrity score is therefore not a universal pass or fail rule for every RNA assay; input, preparation and intended measurement still matter.

notes: RNA integrity concerns molecular condition and fragment distribution, while yield measures recovered quantity. RNases, handling, fixation chemistry and storage can affect recovered molecules. An electropherogram separates size-associated signal. Integrity does not measure malignant-cell share, viability, protein abundance or transcript function.

Schroeder developed RIN from multiple electropherogram features using a trained statistical model. Its 1 to 10 scale runs from degraded to more intact RNA and is not a percentage. DV200 describes measured fragments longer than 200 nucleotides; it does not certify every transcript. In a fictional area illustration, 6 of 10 selected signal-area units above 200 nucleotides give 60%. This is not a computation of RIN or an assay acceptance rule.

Illumina describes DV200 for its RNA enrichment workflows and cautions that RIN can be insensitive in degraded FFPE samples. The older fixed ovarian-tumour study assessed shorter-fragment metrics and library performance because RIN and DV200 did not capture all limitations. Those findings and kit cutoffs must stay with their protocols, rather than becoming universal input rules.

Fictional fixed RNA has low RIN but is accepted for a validated short-target expression assay and rejected for a full-length transcript workflow. These decisions can be consistent because the questions need different evidence. Passing input QC does not establish library complexity or gene recovery; a weak negative can reflect failed recovery rather than biological absence. Gene counts do not prove full-length or splice structure.

RNA quality assessment uses an aliquot of an extract, which itself consumed specimen material. Examine the fragment-size distribution and method-specific quality summary, then check downstream recovery. Report RIN on its 1 to 10 scale, DV200 as a percentage, RNA quantity in nanograms and relevant library or recovery metrics. Acceptance depends on preservation, input amount and the intended assay; there is no universal RIN or DV200 pass cutoff. Poor extraction, degradation, chemical damage, contaminants, insufficient quantity or an uninterpretable trace can limit testing. Integrity does not measure tumour purity, cell viability, protein abundance or transcript function, and a research suitability metric is not a diagnostic result.

records.name: Specimen provenance and derivative tracking
records.tldr: A result needs to remain linked to the tissue or blood sample it came from. Dividing or extracting a specimen creates new material with its own history.
records.summary: NCI guidance describes unique identification of specimens and their derivative samples, with recorded origins and links between parent material, aliquots and extractions. That history helps establish which specimen, preparation and handling conditions produced a measurement. Results from different pieces or time points should not silently be treated as measurements of the same input. Tracking supports interpretation and quality management; it does not make a small sample representative of an entire tumor.

records.name: Messenger RNA construct anatomy
aka: mRNA untranslated regions and poly(A) tail
records.tldr: An engineered messenger RNA includes a protein-coding message and surrounding features that affect how it is used. Those features are part of the construct being tested.
records.summary:
The cap, untranslated regions, coding sequence and poly(A) tail are distinct parts of a messenger RNA construct. A primary dendritic-cell study changed untranslated-region and poly(A)-tail features and measured RNA stability, protein production, peptide display and T-cell stimulation separately. Another experimental study separated effects of codon usage and RNA structure on protein expression. Construct design therefore includes more than the intended amino-acid sequence. A design that improves one measured step in one system does not establish optimal immune effects or clinical efficacy in another.

Start-codon context was tested by single-base substitutions around the AUG initiator in a cloned preproinsulin gene, where the best sequence identified changed proinsulin yield over a 20-fold range (Kozak). The interaction of the cap and the poly(A) tail was tested with luciferase mRNAs delivered by electroporation into tobacco protoplasts, Chinese hamster ovary cells and yeast, where the tail's effect depended on the cap (Gallie). A textbook describes the 5' cap, 5' and 3' untranslated regions that regulate translation initiation and mRNA stability, a poly-A tail of about 200 A residues added by poly-A polymerase to cellular mRNA, and a ribosome that moves from the cap to the AUG, with Kozak's rules describing the sequence around it (OpenStax Biology 2e). The cellular tail length is not a rule for engineered constructs: one dendritic-cell study found that a 120-nucleotide tail, an unmasked tail end and two 3' untranslated regions each improved stability and translation, and it measured transcript amount by RT-PCR, protein by eGFP, peptide-MHC density and T-cell stimulation separately (Holtkamp and colleagues), so a doubled reporter signal after a 3' change is one measurement, not a different antigen or a clinical benefit. These are tested constructs and cell systems, not one best sequence for a clinical product.

records.name: Codon optimization
records.tldr: Synonymous codon changes can preserve the intended protein sequence while changing the RNA message. Their effects need to be measured in the intended expression system.
records.summary:
Primary experiments showed that synonymous codon choices can affect RNA stability and translation. Work on engineered messenger RNAs also separated codon usage from RNA secondary structure, showing that expression depends on more than a simple codon preference. Optimization is a design objective with a particular assay and system, not a guarantee of improved therapy. Changing codons is distinct from choosing which antigen or epitope the construct encodes.

In four human cell lines, three independent methods showed that mRNA stability tracked codon identity rather than nucleotide content, stabilising codons tended to coincide with higher tRNA levels, and the effect depended on translation (Wu and colleagues, 2019). Another study separated codon usage from coding-region structure in eGFP constructs and defined functional half-life as the time an mRNA is actively translated, which differs from RNA that is merely present or protein that persists, so a doubled reporter signal at one time point does not show twice the RNA lifetime, a better neoantigen or any clinical effect (Mauger and colleagues).

notes: A codon is a three-base unit. In the standard genetic code, GCU and GCC both encode alanine; synonymous redesign can preserve the intended amino-acid sequence while altering the RNA. RNA structure, available decoding machinery and experimental conditions still matter. Compare matched RNA amount, chemistry, cap, UTRs, purity and delivery, using RNA and protein time courses and protein identity or activity. A codon score or single reporter measurement cannot establish translation fidelity, peptide display, recognition or benefit, and a changed amino-acid spacer is a different design change.

In Mauger's engineered eGFP constructs, highly expressed messages could have highly structured coding regions, and coding-region structure affected the duration of active translation. This concerns the tested coding regions and does not show that removing every fold or maximising one codon score improves every message.

records.name: Modified nucleosides in messenger RNA
records.tldr: Chemical changes to RNA building blocks can alter how a message is sensed and translated. The effect depends on the RNA and the system in which it is tested.
records.summary:
Primary experiments found that selected nucleoside modifications changed RNA-triggered innate immune activation. Later work showed that purification of modified transcripts also affected inflammatory responses and protein expression. Modification and removal of contaminants are therefore distinct design and manufacturing questions. Results from those experimental systems do not establish that one modification is best for every cancer vaccine, delivery platform or intended immune response.

In cell lines and mice, N1-methylpseudouridine, alone or with 5-methylcytidine, gave higher reporter expression than pseudouridine-based mRNA, up to about 44-fold for double-modified mRNA and about 13-fold for single-modified mRNA as the abstract reports (cell lines and mice respectively), with less innate immunogenicity and better cell viability in vitro (Andries and colleagues). Separately, N1-methylpseudouridine caused +1 ribosomal frameshifting in vitro at slippery sequences, cellular immunity to +1 products was found in mice and humans after vaccination with BNT162b2 vaccine mRNA, and synonymous changes at those sequences reduced frameshifted products; the authors note that no adverse outcomes from mistranslation of the SARS-CoV-2 vaccines have been reported (Mulroney and colleagues). More reporter signal with less cytokine in one matched comparison does not show a stronger antigen-specific T-cell response: unmodified mRNAs were translated better after purification yet still induced high cytokine secretion, and purified modified mRNA was translated 10 to 1000-fold more in primary cells (Karikó and colleagues, 2011), so sensing, expression and T-cell readouts each need their own evidence.

notes: A nucleoside combines a base with a sugar; a nucleotide also carries phosphate. Modified RNA building blocks change chemistry separately from the intended sequence and from contaminating byproducts. Characterise chemistry and identity, impurities, protein identity and quantity, and innate-sensing readouts under matched sequence, amount, cap, UTR, purity and formulation conditions. A translation or cytokine result cannot establish every later immune or clinical outcome.

Karikó's 2005 experiments compared human TLR systems and dendritic-cell readouts under selected nucleoside modifications. In the 2011 study, modified transcripts still contained activating contaminants including double-stranded RNA, and purification changed innate activation and translation. A change in building-block chemistry is therefore separate from removal of byproducts.

records.name: In vitro transcription for RNA products
records.tldr: Enzymes can copy a DNA template into RNA outside a living cell. Producing the transcript is followed by questions about its identity, composition and suitability for use.
records.summary:
Experimental RNA-manufacturing studies distinguish the intended in vitro-transcribed RNA from contaminating products and test how purification affects its performance. A primary RNA-construct study then measured expression and immune stimulation after delivering transcripts to cells. RNA production, product quality and biological performance are separate observations. An RNA yield or a band of the expected size alone does not establish a released product or a clinical treatment effect.

A protocol from authors affiliated with TriLink Biotechnologies describes co-transcriptional capping with the company's CleanCap AG reagent, reported to give 94 per cent cap 1 structure at 5 mg/ml of transcription, against cap 0 products at lower efficiency from first-generation cap analogues (Henderson and colleagues). It describes one reagent and is not a release specification. Separately, T7 polymerase initiated transcription from a promoter-less DNA end and made an antisense strand that paired with the intended RNA as long double-stranded RNA, which stimulated the innate sensor MDA5; the activity was suppressed by modified nucleotides or a lower magnesium concentration (Mu and colleagues). Release analytics are layered: reviews list sequence and modification identity, poly(A) tail, RNA content by UV spectrophotometry, integrity and transcript length by gel or capillary electrophoresis or chromatography, double-stranded RNA by immunoblot or ELISA, and residual DNA as separate attributes; purification has to remove template DNA, unincorporated nucleotides and enzymes; residual nucleotides are controlled below predefined thresholds that need much lower detection limits than the main product, with the intact mRNA itself complicating their detection (Losada and colleagues; Nowak and colleagues). Because RNA content and integrity are separate assays, total mass alone does not show full-length product.

The DNA is a manufacturing input; residual DNA in the product is a separate quality attribute. NEB's IVT evaluation protocol says unincorporated nucleotides and template DNA affect the 260-nanometre absorbance reading and calls for their removal before RNA quantification. This is vendor analytical guidance, not a clinical specification. Record purification and the quantification method separately from transcript length and integrity; total mass alone does not identify full-length RNA.

records.name: Double-stranded RNA impurities
records.tldr: RNA manufacture can also produce unwanted paired RNA material. Measuring and removing it is a product-quality question separate from the intended message.
records.summary:
Primary experiments identified double-stranded RNA among contaminants that affected innate immune activation and translation of in vitro-transcribed messenger RNA. Subsequent work developed and tested a cellulose-based removal method. Those studies support characterizing contaminants and their functional consequences in the tested workflows. They do not establish one universal acceptable impurity level or release method for all RNA products.

One documented origin is T7 polymerase initiating transcription from a promoter-less DNA end, producing an antisense strand and long double-stranded RNA that activated the sensor MDA5 (Mu and colleagues). In purification studies, unmodified mRNAs were translated better after HPLC purification but still induced high levels of cytokine secretion (Karikó and colleagues). A cellulose method removed at least 90 per cent of double-stranded RNA with over 65 per cent recovery regardless of mRNA length, coding sequence or nucleoside composition and increased translation in mice, and agarose gels showed that the purified mRNA stayed intact, but it removed duplexes of 30 base pairs or longer efficiently while most of a 21 base-pair duplex remained (Baiersdörfer and colleagues). Detection has its own scope: that paper notes an earlier report that about 40 base pairs of duplex are needed for detection by the J2 antibody, and a review of mRNA analytics lists immunoblot or ELISA for double-stranded RNA alongside separate integrity assays (Losada and colleagues). A lower dsRNA signal with worse fragmentation or recovery therefore does not show a better product. Method performance in those systems is not a clinical impurity limit.
